source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed all ten final destinations: PostgreSQL 18 EXPLAIN, planner, resource, parallel-plan, comparison, and REL_18_STABLE hash executor sources; MySQL 8.4 hash-join documentation; Graefe's primary survey; and CMU Fall 2023 join notes. Verified current bucket/batch/memory output, per-operation and parallel memory scope, private versus shared Parallel Hash behavior, dynamic batch growth/skew safeguards in source, MySQL applicability, and NULL/distinctness semantics. Current product, source-code, durable research, and instructional claims are separately scoped.

evidence: Checked B, P, equality relation, residual qualification, h and g functions, bucket candidates, join output, page counts, batches, load, and match-state notation.
Checked hash compatibility uses the correct one-way implication: equality requires equal hashes, while equal hashes do not prove equality.
Checked in-memory and Grace cost expressions define every variable and explicitly separate expected, logical-page, and measured quantities.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Hash value, bucket membership, full equality, residual qualification, and final output are never conflated.

evidence: Independently reconstructed parity buckets of sizes one and three and the inner bag with A/x and A/y multiplicity two plus B/z and C/c once.
Recomputed eight left rows, semi A/A/B/C, anti N/D, thirteen candidates, six matches, and seven collision rejections with candidate conservation.
Recomputed the 15,000-page simplified Grace example and the exercise build as 1,440,000,000 bytes or 175,782 8-KiB pages, exceeding 512 MiB before overhead.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Independent evidence is retained in artifacts/reviews/DBE-054/independent-recomputation.txt; modeled pages and bytes are not runtime measurements.

evidence: Reviewed the build/probe prefix invariant and the completeness proof from equality-hash compatibility plus full collision recheck soundness.
Derived partition correctness from equal keys sharing g(h(key)) and disjoint exhaustive batch ownership.
Derived simplified Grace cost as initial read plus partition write plus partition read, approximately three times total input pages.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Expected-linear and external-I/O models are conditional and do not prove uniform hashing, bounded skew, memory residency, or latency.

evidence: Reviewed empty sides, duplicates and many-to-many fanout, NULL and null-safe equality, composite/collated keys, deliberate collisions, residual predicates, and every join kind.
Reviewed tiny/oversized/wide build, load growth, one/many batches, recursive repartition, empty partitions, one heavy key, unavoidable output explosion, and dynamic-filter false positives.

Reviewed worker imbalance, private/shared tables, broadcast/repartition, versioned key encoding, temp corruption/disk-full, cancellation, worker loss, retry/output duplication, spill confidentiality, quotas, and concurrency.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown/incompatible hashing, incomplete filters, corrupt spill, or lost ownership must fall back safely or fail explicitly rather than omit rows.

evidence: Checked every eligible build occurrence is retained or durably owned by exactly one recoverable partition and duplicate rows remain distinct.
Checked full equality/residual/visibility rules every candidate, match flags are per occurrence, and join-kind null extension or early stop is preserved.
Checked partition growth, dynamic filtering, parallel/distributed ownership, memory accounting, ordering, failure, and cleanup obligations.
invariant_checking.notes: Resource policies may change the execution route but cannot weaken the logical bag or failure contract.

evidence: Reviewed in-memory completeness and soundness using build ownership, compatible hashing, bucket traversal, equality, and residual qualification.
Reviewed left/right/full/semi/anti extensions including unmatched probe and per-build-occurrence emission.
Reviewed batch-union equivalence and the exactly-once ownership required across spill growth and retries.
proof_review.notes: The chapter gives algorithm proof obligations, not a proof of every named engine, hash operator class, filesystem, or distributed runtime.

evidence: The executable explicitly labels finite collision/bag evidence and excludes SQL types/collations, MVCC, limits, spill, parallelism, faults, and real performance.
The in-memory model is labeled expected and the Grace formula simplified, with omitted output, recursion, metadata, cache, concurrency, and implementation overhead.
PostgreSQL/MySQL current behavior, stable source observations, research foundations, and teaching derivations are attributed by role and date/version.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No one-batch output, hash function, page formula, or plan shape is presented as universal production proof.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact nine-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded toolchain.
Independent recomputation reproduced buckets, bags, candidates/collisions, Grace pages, build bytes/pages, and comparison invariants.
All ten reference artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-054 and every repository-local link resolved.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS hash join, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, memory/spill run, skew benchmark, dynamic filter, parallel/distributed execution, fault injection, or production workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed progression from equality/hash law through in-memory multimap semantics, collisions and join kinds, memory, Grace/hybrid spill, skew, dynamic filters, parallel/distributed placement, order/pipeline, estimation, failure, and verification. Guarantee, mechanism, implementation, policy, estimate, and observation remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed diagnosis with build/probe rows and widths, key distribution/fanout, buckets/load, batches/growth, memory/temp, worker imbalance, exchange, dynamic filters, concurrency, first/last-row time, and cleanup. Remedies prioritize statistics, filtering, orientation/order, skew isolation, algorithm and workload controls before evidence-based memory changes.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives the compatibility law and state invariants, demonstrates deliberate collisions and bag multiplicity, develops external/parallel/distributed mechanisms, supplies twelve misconceptions and ten distinct examples, and progresses through five exercises to secure distributed design with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, source-code, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, PostgreSQL/MySQL or executor/optimizer maintainer, security, performance, reliability, operations, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither universal equality-hash compatibility for every SQL type/collation/operator, correctness of any named implementation, safe spill/parallel/distributed behavior under every failure, estimator or memory-model accuracy, actual cache/temp/network performance, workload-independent algorithm choice, certification, nor deployment fitness.
